flawed_step: Inferring a universal vertex from 'every edge lies in exactly one triangle'. The Friendship Theorem needs the stronger condition that every pair of vertices has exactly one common neighbour, and the graph is not assumed connected.
counterexample: Two vertex-disjoint triangles: vertices {1,...,6}, edges 12,13,23,45,46,56. The only triangles are {1,2,3} and {4,5,6}, so each edge lies in exactly one triangle. Every vertex has degree 2 < 5, so no vertex is adjacent to all the others.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The disconnected graph made of two disjoint triangles meets the hypothesis, since each edge is in exactly one triangle, but it has no universal vertex.
